concern: F — Rapid aspiration thrombectomy system and method (newer)
title: Rapid aspiration thrombectomy system and method
abstract: Abstract An intravascular access system for facilitation of intraluminal medical procedures within the neurovasculature through an access sheath. The system includes an aspiration or support catheter having a flexible, distal luminal portion having an inner diameter defining a lumen extending between a proximal opening at a proximal end of the luminal portion and a distal opening at a distal end of the luminal portion. The catheter has a rigid spine coupled to at least the proximal end of the luminal portion and extending proximally therefrom. The system includes a dilator having a flexible, distal dilator portion sized to be received within the lumen of the luminal portion. Associated systems, devices, and methods of use are also described.
claims: Claims ( 26 ) What is claimed is: 1. An intravascular access catheter for advancing a medical device for intraluminal medical procedures within a neurovasculature, comprising: a flexible elongate body having a proximal end, a distal-most end, and a single lumen extending therebetween, wherein the flexible elongate body comprises a plurality of regions, wherein one of the plurality of regions is a tapered region, and wherein the distal-most end defines a distal opening from the single lumen; a first marker that is visible under fluoroscopy disposed at a distal end of the tapered region; a second marker that is visible under fluoroscopy disposed at a proximal-most end of the tapered region and configured to identify a maximum outer diameter of the flexible elongate body, wherein the tapered region comprises an unreinforced polymer; and a proximal extension extending proximally from the proximal end of the flexible elongate body to an extracorporeal proximal end, the proximal extension having a lumen communicating with the single lumen of the flexible elongate body forming a single, contiguous lumen between the distal opening and a proximal opening at the extracorporeal proximal end. 2. The intravascular access catheter of claim 1 , wherein the proximal extension is formed of two or more different materials, wherein a first material of the two or more different materials is metal, and wherein a second material of the two or more different materials is polymer, and wherein the two or more different materials are arranged coaxially. 3. The intravascular access catheter of claim 2 , wherein the first material of the two or more different materials is a metal hypotube coated with the polymer. 4. The catheter of claim 2 , wherein the proximal extension has an outer diameter sized to insert through an inner working lumen of an access sheath positioned within a vessel of a patient. 5. The catheter of claim 2 , wherein a proximal end region of the flexible elongate body tapers in outer diameter proximally towards the proximal extension forming a transition section between the flexible elongate body and the proximal extension and an increased outer diameter along a length of the flexible elongate body compared to an outer diameter along a length of the proximal extension. 6. The intravascular access catheter of claim 1 , wherein at least one other region of the plurality of regions of the flexible elongate body comprises unreinforced polymer. 7. The intravascular access catheter of claim 1 , wherein the plurality of regions of the flexible elongate body comprise unreinforced polymer. 8. The intravascular access catheter of claim 1 , wherein the tapered region tapers over a length between 1.5 cm and 3 cm. 9. The intravascular access catheter of claim 1 , wherein the tapered region has a durometer of no more than 35 D. 10. The intravascular access catheter of claim 1 , further including a hub at the extracorporeal proximal end of the proximal extension, the hub includes a lumen in fluid communication with the lumen of the proximal extension. 11. The intravascular access catheter of claim 1 , wherein the lumen of the proximal extension is sized to receive a guidewire between 0.014″ and 0.018″ in diameter. 12. The intravascular access catheter of claim 1 , wherein the tapered region of the flexible elongate body is shapeable by a user. 13. The intravascular access catheter of claim 1 , further comprising a lubricious material incorporated into the unreinforced polymer. 14. The intravascular access catheter of claim 1 , wherein each of the plurality of regions of the flexible elongate body each have a different durometer. 15. The catheter of claim 1 , wherein the first marker is a radiopaque loaded polymer band. 16. The catheter of claim 1 , wherein the distal end of the tapered region is at the distal-most end of the flexible elongate body. 17. The catheter of claim 16 , wherein the flexible elongate body is sufficiently flexible to be advanced distal to a petrous portion of an internal carotid artery. 18. The catheter of claim 1 , wherein the flexible elongate body is sufficiently flexible to be advanced distal to a petrous portion of an internal carotid artery. 19. The catheter of claim 1 , wherein the distal opening from the single lumen is the only distal opening from the single lumen. 20. The access catheter of claim 1 , wherein the maximum outer diameter of the flexible elongate body is sized to form a slip fit with an inner diameter of a catheter being advanced with the intravascular access catheter. 21. A system comprising the access catheter of claim 1 and further comprising a second catheter, the second catheter comprising: a flexible, distal luminal portion having an inner diameter defining a single lumen extending between a proximal opening at a proximal end of the flexible, distal luminal portion and a distal opening at a distal end of the flexible, distal luminal portion; and a control element extending proximally from a point of coupling adjacent the proximal opening of the flexible, distal luminal portion, wherein the control element is configured with sufficient stiffness to control movement of the second catheter, wherein the flexible, distal luminal portion has an outer diameter at the point of coupling that is larger than an outer diameter of the control element at the point of coupling. 22. The system of claim 21 , wherein the intravascular access catheter is configured to insert into the single lumen of the second catheter such that a distal end region of the flexible elongate body extends distally beyond the distal end of the flexible, distal luminal portion of the second catheter. 23. The system of claim 22 , wherein the intravascular access catheter has a length at least as long as a length of the second catheter. 24. The system of claim 22 , wherein a distance between the distal opening of the flexible elongate body and the proximal opening of the proximal extension is sufficient to allow the distal end region of the flexible elongate body to be positioned within the neurovasculature while a proximal end region of the proximal extension is grasped by the user. 25. A system for intraluminal procedures within a neurovasculature comprising: an intravascular access catheter comprising: a flexible elongate body having a proximal end, a distal-most end, and a single lumen extending therebetween, wherein the flexible elongate body comprises a plurality of regions, wherein one of the plurality of regions is a tapered region, and wherein the distal-most end defines a distal opening from the single lumen; a first marker that is visible under fluoroscopy disposed at a distal end of the tapered region; a second marker that is visible under fluoroscopy disposed at a proximal end of the tapered region and configured to identify a maximum outer diameter of the flexible elongate body, wherein the tapered region comprises an unreinforced polymer; and a proximal extension extending proximally from the proximal end of the flexible elongate body to an extracorporeal proximal end, the proximal extension having a lumen communicating with the single lumen of the flexible elongate body forming a single, contiguous lumen between the distal opening and a proximal opening at the extracorporeal proximal end; and an outer catheter comprising a lumen extending between a proximal opening and a distal opening, wherein the lumen of the outer catheter is sized to receive the maximum outer diameter of the flexible elongate body in a slip fit. 26. The system of claim 25 , wherein the flexible elongate body increases in flexibility over its length from a flexibility of the catheter at the proximal end of the tapered region towards a greater flexibility at the distal end of the tapered region.
